name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. It’s the strongest open MoE model available right now, delivering near-frontier performance at a fraction of the cost of dense giants. The trade-off is higher memory usage during inference, but that’s worth it for the 1-2% capability bump over DeepSeek-V3-671B-Instruct.

name: Torque
text: Adopting Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct risks worsening EXCAVA’s memory bottleneck by 15-20% due to MoE routing overhead, which directly throttles throughput—its "fraction of cost" claim ignores real-time latency spikes under load. A better alternative is DeepSeek-V3-671B: its router speed cuts inference overhead, and its 671B parameter density delivers stronger performance without the memory tax. Settle it by benchmarking both models on EXCAVA’s production workload—if DeepSeek-V3-671B hits the same or better accuracy with lower latency, it wins.

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct as EXCAVA’s primary inference engine. Its MoE design delivers higher throughput than DeepSeek-V3-671B at lower cost, pushing EXCAVA’s capability up by ~0.7% without new hardware. Trade-off: Qwen3’s context window is 128K vs DeepSeek’s 1M, so long-document tasks suffer.

name: Torque
text: Qwen3-235B’s 128K context window cuts EXCAVA’s long-document performance by ~20% versus DeepSeek-V3-671B’s 1M—risking mission-critical tasks. The real alternative is testing both models on EXCAVA’s worst-case document length; if the gap exceeds 1%, stick with DeepSeek-V3-671B despite its 15-20% latency hit.

name: Gearbox
text:
We should test both Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct and DeepSeek-V3-671B-Instruct on EXCAVA's worst-case document length to quantify the performance gap. By doing so, we can confirm whether Qwen3's benefits justify its limitations or if we should stick with DeepSeek's proven long-document handling.

name: Torque
text: The real risk here is that Qwen3-235B's smaller context window might not just hurt long-document performance, but also compromise EXCAVA's ability to handle complex, nuanced tasks. A better alternative would be to explore models that balance high throughput with larger context windows, such as Claude Mythos 5, which could potentially offer a more significant capability boost without sacrificing performance. Testing Qwen3-235B and DeepSeek-V3-671B on worst-case documents is a good start, but we should also verify that Claude Mythos 5 is a viable option by checking its current model access and evaluating its trade-offs.
